**Heads up for reviewers — this is complementary to \`/timestamps\`, not a duplicate.**

OpenCode v1.17.13+ shipped the \`session.toggle.timestamps\` keybind ([packages/tui/src/config/keybind.ts:100](../blob/dev/packages/tui/src/config/keybind.ts#L100)) which toggles per-message timestamps next to each individual message in the scrollback ([packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:1426](../blob/dev/packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx#L1426)).

This PR adds the timestamp to a **different** surface: the turn-summary line itself (`▣ agent · model · duration`), which is rendered by `AssistantMessage` and is *not* affected by the \`/timestamps\` toggle. Verified against plain `origin/dev` — the turn-summary line still has no time:

```
▣ Build · gpt-5 · 2.8s          ← current dev
▣ Build · gpt-5 · 2.8s · 3:41 PM ← this PR
```

If maintainers prefer, this could alternatively be gated behind the same \`timestamps\` kv signal so the two surfaces stay consistent — happy to revise in that direction.

Closing as duplicate of #25287 (canonical tracker, OPEN). Same root cause: MCP transport stays `failed` after a transient socket/connection close with no retry/reconnect logic in `convertMcpTool`.

Our PR code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent#6256 addresses the same symptom from the **plugin side** (oh-my-openagent LSP daemon-client: reset `requestWritten=false` on socket close/error so the next call retries) and is complementary to the opencode-core fix proposed in #25287 — they are different layers:

- **#25287** → `packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts` (`convertMcpTool` transport-aware retry) — opencode core, not yet landed
- **code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent#6256** → `daemon-client.ts` close/error handlers — oh-my-openagent plugin, under review

Once #25287 lands at the core, the plugin-side retry becomes a defense-in-depth layer rather than the primary recovery path, but both are independently useful until the upstream fix ships.

Can confirm this was hitting us too — `task` tool subagent dispatch (`subagent_type: "amp-researcher"`, a custom registered agent, not `"general"`) failed 100% reproducibly with:

```
NOT NULL constraint failed: session_message.seq
```

on opencode `1.15.10` (Homebrew, darwin/arm64). Reproduced it multiple ways to rule out other causes:
- Directly via the `task` tool with a custom subagent type
- Via plain `opencode run --model ...` from the CLI
- With a built-in `subagent_type: "general"` and a trivial no-tool prompt (so not specific to our custom agent registration or MCP tools)

Also ruled out DB/process contention as the cause — we had ~30 unrelated stale/zombie `opencode run` processes (leftover scheduled jobs) holding handles on the same SQLite file, killed them all, and the error persisted identically afterward with only one process attached to the DB. So in our case it wasn't lock contention, just this constraint bug on the new-session insert path, consistent with the `COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1` root cause described above.

**Update:** upgraded from `1.15.10` → `1.18.4` and the exact same subagent dispatch now works cleanly — verified with a live subagent successfully calling MCP tools and returning results, no errors. Whatever landed between those versions fixed it for us. Leaving this here in case it helps confirm the fix version for others still on `1.15.x`.

The continuous loop and context loss you are experiencing with the opencode/big-pickle model stems from a critical upstream routing bug coupled with state-handling errors in OpenCode's engine.The Big Pickle stealth model (which routes through the OpenCode Zen endpoint) frequently trips over tool completion detection. This creates an infinite loop that completely wipes the sliding window context mid-session, blowing past your rate limits and quota.

﻿## Update: Root cause found — `HTTP_PROXY` pointing at a dead proxy + Bun ignoring `NO_PROXY`

After further investigation, the root cause is **not** Bun being unable to connect to localhost per se. It's a combination of two issues:

### 1. `HTTP_PROXY` env var pointing at a dead proxy

The `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables were set to `http://127.0.0.1:7555` — a proxy port that **was not running**. This meant every outbound HTTP request from opencode was being sent to a dead proxy.

### 2. Bun runtime ignores `NO_PROXY` (confirmed: #37043)

Even though `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost,::1` was set, opencode's embedded Bun runtime **ignored it** and routed the `http://127.0.0.1:9877/v1` request through the `HTTP_PROXY` at `127.0.0.1:7555` — which was dead. This is exactly the bug described in #37043.

This explains why **both** local (`127.0.0.1:9877`) and public (`https://models.dev/api.json`) URLs failed with the same "Unable to connect" error — they were all being sent to the dead 7555 proxy.

### Why it was intermittent

The 7555 proxy was sometimes running (e.g., briefly after a reboot when a proxy app started then crashed, or when switching proxy configurations). When 7555 happened to be up, opencode worked. When it was down, everything failed. This matched the observed pattern where some providers (openai, ollama, deepseek) had high but not 100% success rates — they succeeded when 7555 was briefly alive.

### Fix

Changed `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` to point at the actually-running proxy (`http://127.0.0.1:60230` in this case). After restarting opencode from a terminal with the corrected env vars, the `commandcode` provider at `http://127.0.0.1:9877/v1` connects successfully and reliably.

### Key takeaway for maintainers

The user-facing error "Cannot connect to API: Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url?" is misleading when the real cause is `HTTP_PROXY` pointing at a dead proxy + `NO_PROXY` being ignored. Two improvements would help:

1. **Respect `NO_PROXY` for loopback addresses** (fix #37043) — this would have made the local proxy work regardless of `HTTP_PROXY` state.
2. **Better error messaging** — when `FailedToOpenSocket` occurs on a proxy URL (not the destination URL), the error should indicate the proxy is unreachable, not the destination. Something like "Unable to connect to proxy at http://127.0.0.1:7555 — is the proxy running?" would have made this trivial to diagnose.

This issue can likely be closed as a duplicate of #37043 (NO_PROXY ignored), with the added context that the impact is broader than just loopback — any dead `HTTP_PROXY` causes all providers to fail silently.

Independent field validation of this fix — LGTM.

**Environment**: long-running deployment with a large shared session database (~17 GB, WAL), several concurrent client processes writing to the same canonical DB, and a filesystem that was at ~98-99% utilization.

**Symptom observed (matches #36578 exactly)**: repeated `Failed to execute statement` log lines with the real SQLite cause swallowed — including one burst of failures across 4 sessions within ~26 seconds. After freeing disk space the errors stopped recurring, which is consistent with the `SQLITE_FULL` path this PR surfaces (with concurrent writers `SQLITE_BUSY` is also plausible for us — the sanitized `(CODE)` form is exactly what we need to disambiguate on the next occurrence).

**What I did**: first applied a raw `cause.message` stopgap at the same two `sqlite.bun.ts` hunks, then replaced it with this PR's approach on a v1.18.4-based branch — `executeErrorMessage` in `sqlite.ts`, both `sqlite.bun.ts`/`sqlite.node.ts` call sites, `MessageV2.sqlErrorMessage`, and the `processor.ts` halt logging change.

**Verification**:
- `tsgo --noEmit` clean in `packages/core` and `packages/opencode`
- `database-sqlite.test.ts`: 2/2 pass
- `message-v2.test.ts`: 37/37 pass (including the new "surfaces SQLite details without query parameters" test)
- Deployed binary serves normally; new message strings present, old fixed string gone

One minor note: the `bus/global.ts` EventEmitter change is unrelated to the sqlite fix (understood it's needed for the current dev typecheck) — might be worth splitting so this PR stays focused, but not a blocker.

> **Disclosure: this comment was written and the analysis performed by an LLM — Claude (Fable 5) running in Claude Code — posted with review and approval by the account owner (@thecatfix).** The OP asks not to post LLM-suggested solutions; everything below is snapshot measurements and a reproducible driver, with one optional suggestion clearly marked. Discount it accordingly.

## ~73k permanently-Open Effect Scopes: fixed boot overhead, built twice — measured, with repro

Measurements only, from heap snapshots + a source-level repro driver against v1.18.0 (`32696c4`). Not runtime growth — a fixed ~36–42 MiB overhead that the TUI pays twice.

### What the snapshot shows

A TUI session's `server.heapsnapshot` (macOS arm64, v1.18.0) holds **73,352 Effect Scope objects, all `state._tag: "Open"`** — 62,043 with `strategy: "sequential"`, 11,309 `"parallel"`. Each is a `scopeForkUnsafe` pair (child-close finalizer in parent's Map + remove-finalizer in child's Map), so it also drives the Map count (1.3k → 75k vs TUI baseline) and ~35–42 MiB of retained closures/Maps.

### Repro (from source, no LLM guessing — counted from snapshots)

Driver runs `Server.Default().app` in-process, hits endpoints, writes `node:v8` `writeHeapSnapshot` after each phase, and a script counts objects with `strategy`+`state` properties:

| condition | Open scopes (seq/par) |
|---|---|
| `Server.Default()` app built, one warm-up request | **36,326** (30,741 / 5,585) |
| +150× `GET /global/health` | +0 |
| +150× `GET /config` | +53 |
| +150× `GET /api/health?directory=…` | +0 |
| +150× `GET /api/session?directory=…` | +0 |
| +1 workspace instance boot | +0 |
| +2 workspace instance boots | +0 |
| + `Server.listen()` on top of `Default()` | **72,696** |

72,696 ≈ the 73,352 in the real TUI snapshot (same 5.5:1 strategy ratio). So the count is two full route-layer-graph builds, not accumulation.

### Where the two builds come from

1. TUI worker uses `Server.Default()` (in-process `webHandler`) for its own `rpc.fetch`.
2. It also starts the TCP listener: `startListener` → `Layer.buildWithMemoMap(listenerLayer(...), Layer.makeMemoMapUnsafe(), scope)` (`packages/opencode/src/server/server.ts:126`) — a **fresh memoMap**, so every service builds a second time. This also duplicates service state; e.g. the same snapshot holds ~17.2k model-catalog objects vs ~5.8k in the TUI process — consistent with ~2× duplication.

Each build produces ~36.3k scope pairs because `LayerNode.compile` emits `implementation.pipe(Layer.provide(deps))` per node (`packages/core/src/effect/layer-node.ts:263`), and every `Layer.provide` edge goes through `mergeAllEffect`, which forks 1 `"parallel"` + N `"sequential"` scopes (`effect/dist/Layer.js`, `mergeAllEffect`) that stay Open for the server's lifetime.

### Possible one-line reduction (take or leave)

`routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts` already has a module-level `memoMap` used by `webHandler`, and `routes = createRoutes()` is a module singleton. Passing that same `memoMap` in `server.ts:126` instead of `Layer.makeMemoMapUnsafe()` makes the listener's build hit cache for the whole inner graph — removing ~36k scopes and the duplicated service instances. The remaining ~36k per build is the shape of the compiled layer graph itself.

### Side observation

While driving `/api/event` in-process, aborting the SSE fetch never tears down the stream — the driver wedged, which matches #36739.

Adding a new failure-mode variant to this thread: the same root family (bash→stream lifecycle race, glm-5.2 via opencode-go) but instead of a silent hang, the session enters a **runaway 860× empty-bash-error loop** that burns the user's entire token allocation in ~50 minutes with zero useful work. The user-visible symptom is the opposite of #33028's silent hang — it's a fast, complete saturation of usage, with no visibility from the user side.

## Environment
- opencode-ai: 1.18.4 (current stable)
- Provider: ollama-cloud (model: glm-5.2)
- OS: Linux
- Mode: subagent (gsd-executor spawned via the Task tool, mode=subagent)

## Session
- `ses_07ac7c5acffeTSx06Xa5uPkBxS` ("Execute plan 13-01")
- 2836 parts total; 860 of them are `bash` tool calls with `command: ""` and the same error.

## The new symptom: runaway empty-bash loop (not a silent hang)

After a normal bash call completed at 16:15:42 (`callID functions.bash:69`, a real pytest signature check), the subagent began emitting `bash` tool calls with `command: ""`. Each returned the same error:

```json
{
  "type": "tool",
  "tool": "bash",
  "callID": "functions.bash:70",
  "state": {
    "status": "error",
    "input": { "command": "" },
    "error": "The argument 'file' cannot be empty. Received ''",
    "metadata": { "output": "" }
  }
}
```

860 such calls followed, every 2–4 seconds, for 51 minutes (16:15:46 → 17:10:58), until the user hard-stopped the session. Every one has the identical error message. The `callID` increments each time (functions.bash:70, :71, :72 …), so these are distinct tool invocations from the model, not a single retry. The model fell into a degenerate state where every emitted tool call was an empty bash; the harness kept accepting and erroring on them instead of terminating the turn.

## Why this is a different user-visible failure mode from #33028

#33028 reports a **silent hang** — the next stream never produces output, no `error=Aborted` ever fires, the session is quiet and stuck. Our case is the opposite: the harness keeps firing `error` back at the model every 2–4 seconds, the model keeps emitting another empty bash, and the loop is tight and noisy — but the user sees nothing on the terminal because the orchestrator is blocked on the Task call waiting for the subagent to return. So:

- **#33028:** silent, stuck, no tokens burned while stuck.
- **This variant:** not silent to the provider — 860 LLM round-trips, ~152M input tokens re-sent on every empty-bash call (full conversation context compounding), zero useful work, **drains a $100/5hr ollama tier by ~40% in 50 minutes**.

Both variants share the same root cause (bash→stream lifecycle race, no stream timeout, no empty-arg pre-execution guard). The fix proposed in this thread (stream timeout + `awaitToolFibers` timeout) would address both; the empty-arg pre-execution guard proposed in #27871 would specifically stop the runaway variant, because the loop depends on the harness accepting the empty `command: ""` and returning an error rather than rejecting it before execution.

## The "file cannot be empty" error wording is suspicious

The error on every empty-bash call is:

```
The argument 'file' cannot be empty. Received ''
```

The `bash` tool does not take a `file` argument — it takes `command`. That wording suggests the empty `command` is being routed through a validator that expects a `file` parameter (the `read` tool's schema, or a shared validator). Worth a look at the bash tool's input-validator path.

## Reproduction evidence (pulled from the opencode SQLite db)

`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, table `part`, session `ses_07ac7c5acffeTSx06Xa5uPkBxS`:

- 2836 parts total
- 860 parts with `type: "tool"`, `tool: "bash"`, `state.status: "error"`, `state.input.command: ""`, all with the identical error `"The argument 'file' cannot be empty. Received ''"`
- The 51-minute burn window: 16:19:36 onward is uninterrupted empty-bash-errors (no real tools, no reasoning parts, no edits —

This is still very much alive on opencode 1.17.20 (2026-07-21), on a real project — not just the synthetic repro. Auto-closed by the 60-day stale bot with `state_reason: not_planned`, but nothing was actually fixed.

Reproduction, from `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`:

Config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`):
```json
"permission": {
  "external_directory": {
    "*": "ask",
    "/tmp/opencode/**": "allow"
  }
}
```

Headless review subagents (`mode: subagent`, no interactive prompt available) tried to read a diff file written to `/tmp/opencode/<lineage>.diff`. Log:

```
evaluated permission=external_directory pattern=/tmp/opencode/* action.pattern=* action.action=deny
```

The `/tmp/opencode/**` rule never matches because (per the source referenced in this issue) `external_directory` always checks against `path.join(dir, "*")` — a fixed single-star suffix — not the actual file path. Since the specific allow rule can't match, it falls through to the `"*": "ask"` catch-all, and since the subagent is headless, unresolved `ask` degrades to `deny`. Same root cause as #14445 and the general glob-matching issue in #22465.

Workaround that unblocked us: add an extra literal-single-star entry alongside the globstar one:
```json
"/tmp/opencode/**": "allow",
"/tmp/opencode/*": "allow"
```

Reopening would help — this is a genuine footgun for anyone using headless/subagent review pipelines with external_directory rules, not resolved by the closure.

Regression in Desktop 1.18.4 (Windows 11 + WSL2, `Ubuntu-26.04`). The fix from #37890 is included in the installed release, but startup still fatally crashes with the same error.

Current exported debug bundle timeline:
```text
20:33:16.587  Desktop 1.18.4 starting
20:33:18.055  WSL sidecar starting: wsl:Ubuntu-26.04
20:33:19.106  FATAL renderer: Notification server not found: wsl:Ubuntu-26.04
20:33:20.199  WSL sidecar ready: wsl:Ubuntu-26.04
```

So this is the same transient sidecar-readiness condition, not a failing WSL server. The stack is now through `ProjectAvatar` / `HomeSessionRow` and identifies `ensure` *as* `ensureServerState`:
```text
Error: Notification server not found: wsl:Ubuntu-26.04
  at Object.ensure [as ensureServerState] (...)
  at Object.fn (...)
  at ProjectAvatar (...)
  at SessionTabAvatar (...)
  at HomeSessionRow (...)
```

`#37890` only changed `selected()` to fall back when the active key is not in `global.servers.list()`. However `packages/app/src/pages/layout/project-avatar-state.ts` bypasses `selected()`:
```ts
notification.ensureServerState(server()).session.unseenCount(sessionId())
```

and in `v1.18.4`, `ensure()` still contains:
```ts
if (!conn) throw new Error(`Notification server not found: ${key}`)
```

Thus any restored/home session row for a configured WSL server can still crash the renderer before that sidecar is registered. The direct API needs the same non-throwing fallback/no-op behavior (or callers must guard the connection), rather than relying on the `selected()` fallback alone.

The previously proposed fallback in unmerged/closed #37190 appears to address this direct-call path. A regression test should exercise `useSessionTabAvatarState` (or another direct `ensureServerState(wslKey)` consumer) while the WSL sidecar is configured but not yet ready.
